page: Amazon Web Services m6i.24xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The system is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at a base clock of 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 instruction set. It provides 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs utilizing simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core. Hardware security and instruction features include AVX-512, SHA-NI, AES-NI, and Total Memory Encryption. System memory comprises 384 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, providing a standard balanced allocation of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance incorporates 38 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth. It includes no bundled local NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallelized processing performance, with multi-core tests consistently placing in the top 25% of evaluated systems. The platform achieved a multi-core stress-ng result of 92,891.39 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,513.0, supported by large-block uncached read memory bandwidth of 326.83 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 139.2 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is particularly high, ranking in the top 10% on PassMark encryption tests at 86,924.21. In contrast, single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1,641.0) and single-core stress-ng (1,892.78), remain in the middle 50% performance bracket.

The hardware configuration provides favorable resource density for scale-up concurrent tasks without specialized accelerator overhead. The instance performs strongly on high-throughput data tasks, demonstrated by 89.19 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and static web throughput of 61.47 GB/sec. Architectural tradeoffs involve the lack of ephemeral local storage, requiring network-attached storage configurations for persistent disk operations. Additionally, without discrete GPU hardware, performance drops significantly on intensive large-parameter AI text generation, recording 2.71 tokens per second on 70B models. The configuration is best aligned with enterprise web serving, large caching arrays, parallel Clang compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded database workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m6i.24xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at 3.5 GHz. It features 384 GB of DDR4 system memory at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, alongside 38 Gbps of baseline networking throughput. The instance includes no bundled local storage or hardware accelerators, utilizing network storage for disk operations. In benchmarks, the m6i.24xlarge delivers strong multi-core compute throughput, high memory bandwidth, and top-tier cryptographic performance, while single-threaded tasks perform in the average range. With 89.19 million operations per second in Redis tests and 61.47 GB/sec web serving throughput, the system is suited for enterprise web serving, large-scale multi-threaded software compilation, in-memory caching layers, and concurrent backend services.
